decisions.reason: The candidate already records the same-message requirement that both stations operate simultaneously. The several-minute acceptance criterion is a separate machine-level reliability condition and does not necessarily require both stations to remain simultaneous for that entire duration.

The source separately requests working speed adjustment and several minutes of continuous operation; it does not change the speed range, maximum speed, independent control behavior, or normal speed usage.
Continuous operation for several minutes does not change the existing splash-control target, methods, or high-speed cleanliness requirement.
The source does not modify the required matcha texture, foam quality, smoothness, or high-speed mixing behavior.
The continuous-operation acceptance criterion does not change the whisk head's size, material, style, powder compatibility, or positioning.
The source does not alter whisk removability, detachment speed, or the preference for tool-free removal.

The several-minute whole-machine demonstration does not change the selected 120V architecture, supply rating, controller capacity, or existing requirement to support all electrical loads without overload or overheating.
The source acknowledges that the machine is sturdy but does not change the existing structural rigidity or vibration-control requirements.
The functional continuous-operation criterion does not resume or modify the deferred DJ-style visual details.
The source's continuous-operation acceptance criterion does not change food-path cleaning, sanitation, removability, or hidden-liquid-trap requirements.
The source does not resolve, resume, or modify the deferred LED-lighting requirement; the functional demonstration remains independent of cosmetic lighting.

Although the message separately requests dispensing through both spouts, the continuous-operation modification does not change spout location, orientation, geometry, fabrication style, or pour direction.
